thread:
elaine: Quick idea 1: 'flex windows' for Reserved Pools. Customers opt in to scheduled capacity reductions (e.g., 30-60%) during predictable low-traffic periods in exchange for a usage credit. Target workloads: nightly batches, offline embeddings. Thoughts?

mike: Is this a per-tenant recurring schedule or one-off windows? How will autoscale interact?

elaine: MVP: recurring per-tenant schedule (supports multiple windows, timezone-aware). Autoscale still runs but headroom is capped inside the window.

sara: Ops: need auto-escape if SLOs degrade. Otherwise after a while we'll have noisy pages.

jason: Legal/product needs clear contract language "scheduled lower-capacity windows" + fallback guarantees. Also: launch criteria = 2 pilot customers + runbook + billing spec.

adrian: Implementation note: model windows as admission policy objects. During active window, admission controller reduces rate token bucket and signals runtime to reduce batch-size hints. Fallback: route to hosted model variant or allow temporary burst credit.

hana: Acme Analytics is interested: they'd accept 40% throughput cut 01:00-05:00 local for ~25% monthly credit.

mike: Edge case: combine with preemption or other throttles. Need deterministic priority resolution for conflicting policies.

adrian: Priority: safety overrides (latency or error triggers) > emergency operator override > scheduled flex window. So windows are lowest priority but reversible automatically.

sara: Suggested safety thresholds: p95 > 2x SLO for 3m -> auto-fallback; error-rate > 5% for 5m -> notify + fallback; manual abort in Console.

jason: Console/API surface: toggle opt-in, calendar view of windows, credit preview, audit trail. API route: POST /reserved_pools/{id}/flex_windows.

elaine: Example API payload:

```
POST /api/v1/reserved_pools/123/flex_windows
{
  "recurrence": "RRULE:FREQ=DAILY",
  "start_time": "01:00",
  "end_time": "05:00",
  "throughput_multiplier": 0.6,
  "discount_pct": 25,
  "timezone": "America/Los_Angeles",
  "safety": {"p95_latency_ms": 2000, "error_rate_pct": 5}
}
```

mike: Runtime question: caching effects. Throttling may increase evictions and tail latency. Need simulation and a cache_weight hint so runtime prefers short-lived hot entries during windows.

adrian: Good call. We'll add cache hints to the policy and run a simulation to predict tail impact. Also admission controller will emit telemetry for actual vs predicted tail latency.

hana: Billing: prefer pro-rata per-window credit added to monthly invoice. Also pilot should include an opt-out clause if regressions occur.

jason: Agreed pro-rata per-window. Add opt-out and trial terms to pilot contract.

elaine: Proposed launch checklist:
- 2 enterprise pilots (sales to secure)
- admission controller + safety triggers implemented (RFC + small canary)
- Console scheduling UI + API MVP
- billing flow for per-window credits
- runbook and one-click abort in Console
- 2-week internal canary + 1-week customer pilot

sara: Add oncall drill + alerting thresholds and test plan.

mike: Rough engineering estimate: 3 sprints admission/controller, 2 sprints Console work, 1 sprint billing and telemetry. Depends on priorities.

elaine: Action items: @adrian write RFC for admission semantics and safety signals; @mike run cache/latency simulation; @jason draft pilot contract and billing terms; @sara draft runbook and drills; @hana confirm Acme pilot interest. ops-bot: create tickets?

ops-bot: Created tickets IRIS-8801 (admission RFC), IRIS-8802 (console flex windows UI), IRIS-8803 (billing credits flow), IRIS-8804 (runbook + drills).

elaine: Thanks all 1. I'll sync with Sales to firm up pilots and follow up next Tue. If anyone wants to reprioritize this, flag now. :thumbsup:
